question_en: Which of the following is a challenge that alternative investments have?
option_a: Same information between managers and investors.
explanation_en: It is difficult to assess performance for alternative investments because historical return and volatility data is less available compared to traditional investments. Alternative investments typically have low correlation with traditional investments and managers have different information than investors.

subtopic: Reading 78 Alternative Investment Features, Methods, and Structures
question_en: Victrix is a hedge fund that has a 3-and-15 fee structure. Compared to hedge funds with 2- and-20 fee structures, Victrix charges higher:
explanation_en: Hedge fund fee structures indicate management fees as a percentage of assets under management and incentive fees as a percentage of gains in value. A 3-and-15 fee structure means a fund charges a 3% management fee and a 15% incentive fee.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Alternative Investment\Reading 78 Alternative Investment Features, Methods, and Structures - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 78 Alternative Investment Features, Methods, and Structures
question_en: The most likely perceived benefit of alternative investments is:
explanation_en: Perceived benefits of alternative investments include (1) risk reduction from diversification since alternative investments tend to have low correlations with traditional investments, and (2) possible higher returns from holding illiquid securities. Alternative investments are generally more difficult to access because of higher minimum investments and specialized knowledge.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Alternative Investment\Reading 78 Alternative Investment Features, Methods, and Structures - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 78 Alternative Investment Features, Methods, and Structures
question_en: An alternative investment fund generated an 18% return during 20X2. The manager has a 20% performance fee, subject to an 8% soft hurdle rate and a catch-up clause. What performance fee did the manager earn for 20X2?
explanation_en: The investor would receive the first 8%. The catch-up would allow the manager to receive the next 2%, so it catches up on earning 20% of the first 10% of gains. The manager will also receive another 20% of the 8% remaining after the catch-up, which is 1.6%. Thus, the manager would earn 2% + 1.6% = 3.6%.

subtopic: Reading 78 Alternative Investment Features, Methods, and Structures
question_en: What is another name for a performance fee paid by investors in alternative investment funds?
explanation_en: The performance fee may also be called an incentive fee or carried interest. This fee is designed to incentivize management based on performance, and typically the fund must exceed a hurdle rate or preferred return before that performance fee is earned. Fund managers earn the management fee regardless of performance.

question_en: Hedge fund management fees are most commonly structured as a percentage of:
explanation_en: For hedge funds, management fees are calculated as a percentage of assets under management— typically, the net asset value of the fund. For private capital funds, the management fee is calculated as a percentage of committed capital.

question_en: A private equity provision that requires managers to return any periodic incentive fees resulting in investors receiving less than 80% of profits is a:
explanation_en: A clawback provision requires the manager to return any periodic incentive fees to investors that would result in investors receiving less than 80% of the profits generated by portfolio investments as a whole.

subtopic: Reading 78 Alternative Investment Features, Methods, and Structures
question_en: Which private capital fund waterfall structure involves distributing profits as each investment is sold and subsequently shared according to the partnership agreement?
explanation_en: With a deal-by-deal waterfall, profits are distributed as each fund investment is sold and subsequently shared according to the partnership agreement. With a whole-of-fund waterfall (or European waterfall), the limited partners receive all distributions until they have received 100% of their initial investment plus the hurdle rate.

subtopic: Reading 78 Alternative Investment Features, Methods, and Structures
question_en: Which alternative investment incentive fee feature is most likely to benefit the manager?
explanation_en: A catch-up clause allows the manager to catch up on its performance fee after the hurdle rate is reached. A high-water mark disallows performance fees on gains that only offset prior losses. A clawback provision returns prior performance fees to investors if gains are reversed when deals are exited.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Alternative Investment\Reading 78 Alternative Investment Features, Methods, and Structures - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 78 Alternative Investment Features, Methods, and Structures
question_en: Compared to fund investing, direct investing most likely has:
explanation_en: Direct investing avoids outside manager fees, while fund managers charge fees. Disadvantages of direct investing include lack of diversification, higher required investment amounts, and specialized knowledge needed to evaluate deals. Fund investing provides access to a more diversified pool of assets, and the investment amount is typically lower because the cost is shared with other investors.

explanation_en: A hedge fund typically is more likely to use leverage, is less liquid, and charges higher fees than a traditional mutual fund.

subtopic: Reading 79 Alternative Investment Performance and Returns
question_en: Carr Funds is a hedge fund with $125 million of assets under management at the end of the prior year. The fund has a "1 and 10" fee structure. Incentive fees are calculated on gains net of management fees at the end of the year. In the current year, Carr Funds had a 5% gross return. An investor's after-fee return for the year is closest to:
explanation_en: Gross value end of year: $125 million × 1.05 = $131.25 million Management fee: $131.25 million × 1% = $1.3125 million Incentive fee: ($131.25 – $125 – $1.3125) × 10% = $493,750 Total fees to Carr Funds = $1.3125 million + $493,750 = $1,806,250 The after-fee return: [($131.25 – $1.80625) / 125] – 1 = 3.56%.

subtopic: Reading 79 Alternative Investment Performance and Returns
question_en: Jem Capital is a hedge fund with $150 million of initial investment capital. The fund charges a 2% management fee based on assets under management at the end of the year and a 20% incentive fee. Incentive fees and management fees are calculated independently. In the first year, Jem Capital has a 25% return. What is an investor's after-fee return for the year?
explanation_en: Gross value end of year: $150 million × 1.25 = $187.5 million Management fee: $187.5 million × 2% = $3.75 million Incentive fee: ($187.5 million – $150 million) × 20% = $7.5 million Total fees to Jem Capital: $11.25 million The after-fee return: [(187.5 – 11.25) / 150] – 1 = 17.5%.

subtopic: Reading 79 Alternative Investment Performance and Returns
question_en: A hedge fund has a 2-and-20 fee structure with a soft hurdle rate of 5% and a high water mark. Incentive fees are calculated net of management fees. The fund's gross return is 15% in Year 1, −10% in Year 2, and 30% in Year 3. Incentive fees for Year 3 will be:
option_a: less than 20% of the increase in value in Year 3 after management fees.
option_b: equal to 20% of the increase in value in Year 3 after management fees.
option_c: greater than 20% of the increase in value in Year 3 after management fees.
explanation_en: Because the fund lost value in Year 2 and has a high water mark, incentive fees for Year 3 will be 20% of only the portion of the Year 3 gain that exceeds the previous highest value.

subtopic: Reading 80 Investments in Private Capital- Equity and Debt
question_en: Which of the following types of private debt has the lowest level of risk?
explanation_en: Unitranche debt is a blend of different classes of debt and typically ranks between senior and subordinated debt. Mezzanine debt is subordinated to senior debt and often unsecured. Venture debt is the riskiest because it finances start-up companies that have high business risk and often lack positive cash flow and assets.

question_en: The formative stage of venture capital investing when capital is furnished for market research and product development is best characterized as the:
explanation_en: In the seed stage of venture capital investing, capital is furnished for product development, marketing, and market research. The angel investing stage is when investment funds are used for business plans and assessing market potential. The early stage refers to investments made to fund initial commercial production and sales.
